intro:
Escape from Capua — 73 BC

Spartacus, the school at Capua is behind you, but the roads ahead still belong to Rome. The fugitives have only the weapons they could seize in the escape. If the local guards gather before you reach open country, they can surround the whole band.

Get your people out towards Vesuvius. Keep them together until the pursuit is shaken off; shelter and new followers can be found once you are clear of the town.

intro:
Gathering the fugitives — 73 BC

Freedom will not last without food and weapons. The estates around Capua hold both, and other enslaved people are looking for a chance to join you. Local guards still control the roads between them.

Take the settlements and supply points around the camp. Gather the new arrivals under Spartacus, Crixus and Oenomaus, and leave enough fighters with the supplies to protect them. Rome's response will be stronger than the men you escaped at the school.

intro:
Vesuvius — 73 BC

Glaber has blocked the approaches to Vesuvius. He expects hunger to bring you down from the mountain, and the Roman camp below is preparing for a siege.

Find a way through the cordon and strike the besiegers' positions. The mountain has sheltered the band; now it threatens to become a prison. Break the Roman force before more troops arrive to close the remaining paths.

intro:
Nola — 73 BC

The band has grown beyond what its first refuges can feed. Nola offers stores, weapons and the prospect of new followers, but its garrison still holds the gates and approaches.

Gather the fighters and take the town before the Roman response catches up with you. Keep watch on the roads while the supplies are collected. We cannot afford to be shut inside the very place that is meant to sustain the march.

intro:
Acerrae: Furius — 73 BC

Varinius is bringing another Roman army against us, but his detachments are still separated. Furius has come within reach near Acerrae before the main body can support him.

Overrun his position while he stands alone. Keep watch on the roads from the Roman army; once their columns join, the chance to defeat them separately will be gone.

intro:
The camp of Cossinius — 73 BC

Cossinius has brought his detachment ahead of Varinius's main army. His camp near Herculaneum is exposed, and the men who might relieve it are still some distance away.

Strike the camp and secure its approaches before the Romans can regroup. The weapons and supplies will strengthen our own force, and Varinius will have one fewer column with which to close around us.

intro:
Escape from Varinius — 73 BC

Varinius has brought up his main army. Our camp is becoming a trap: each day behind its defences consumes food while the Roman lines grow stronger.

Open a passage and lead the band out through the cordon. Leave a rearguard between the Roman main body and the withdrawing columns until the slower groups are clear. If the passage cannot be opened at once, hold the camp together while another attempt is prepared.

intro:
Nuceria — 73 BC

The band has escaped, but Varinius is still following. Nuceria lies ahead, with the stores we need and people who may join the rising.

Take the town and the positions controlling its approaches. Keep the pursuit away while the columns gather supplies and move through. We need to leave Nuceria stronger than we entered it, before the Romans can pin us against its walls.

intro:
Picentia: turn on Varinius — 73 BC

Varinius will give us no peace. Every halt for food or recruits allows his army to close the distance, and the march cannot continue indefinitely with his troops at our backs.

Turn on the pursuit near Picentia. Seize its positions and break the Roman detachments before they can gather into a single line. Defeating this army would give the rising room to move beyond Campania.

intro:
Spartacus or Crixus — 72 BC

The camp no longer agrees on where freedom lies. Spartacus's followers look towards a road out of Italy; Crixus's group intends to continue the struggle here. The two columns are preparing to separate.

Choose which leader to follow and move to his assembly point. Your force will march with that column in the battles ahead.

intro:
Mons Garganus: Crixus — 72 BC

Crixus, Rome has sent consular armies against the rising. Arrius's troops are ahead of Gellius's main force near Mount Garganus, and they threaten to pin your column while the rest of the Romans come up.

Attack their camp and take the surrounding positions before they can close around you. Spartacus is marching with his own followers; leave him with that column and fight this battle with yours.

intro:
Gellius: Crixus's continuation (alternate history) — 72 BC

Crixus, the victory over Arrius has bought time, but Gellius is bringing the main Roman army towards you. His columns threaten the roads through Siponto and Herdonia.

Take those positions and break the ring before it closes. Keep your own column together; Spartacus must remain with his separate force. The Romans expect the first victory to have left your men scattered over their spoils.

intro:
Lentulus blocks the road — 72 BC

Spartacus, Lentulus stands across the northern road, and another Roman army is approaching from behind. If the consuls unite, they can force you to fight on both fronts.

Break Lentulus's line at Cliternia and open the road for the main body. Keep a rearguard facing the pursuit until the column is through. Crixus commands a separate force and must not be brought into this march.

intro:
Turn against Gellius — 72 BC

Lentulus has been driven back, but Gellius is still following from the south. News of Crixus's defeat has reached the camp. His column cannot come to our aid.

Turn on the pursuers and take their positions while holding Cliternia. Strike before Gellius can join the troops already beaten on the northern road. The surviving army needs room to continue its march.

intro:
Cisalpine Gaul — 72 BC

The Alps are closer, but another Roman force stands across the route. Cassius holds the approaches through Mutina and Regium Lepidum, barring the way out of Cisalpine Gaul.

Break his line and take the towns and their approaches. Keep the column together until the passage is secure. The prospect of leaving Italy will count for little if the Romans can cut the march in two here.

intro:
Firmum Picenum — 72 BC

The army is marching south again. Roman forces are gathering across the roads of Picenum, and every delay gives them time to bring another column against us.

Take Firmum Picenum, Ancona and Auximum, and secure the positions linking them. The army needs these roads and stores to sustain its march. Keep the passage open while the main body moves through.

intro:
Break Crassus's cordon — 71 BC

The pirates have taken their payment without bringing the ships. Sicily is beyond our reach, supplies are running down, and Crassus's fortifications seal the land route out of southern Italy.

Force a passage through the Roman cordon and bring the army out. Hold the breach while the slower columns pass, then pull the rearguard through. No fleet is coming; we must open our own road north.

intro:
Relieve the separated camp — 71 BC

Castus and Gannicus have separated from the main army. Crassus is moving against their camp, hoping to destroy them before Spartacus can intervene.

March to their relief and secure the positions around Metapontum, Heraclea and Grumentum. Hold the roads between the two forces so the Romans cannot isolate them again. The separated troops need a way back to the army, not another column trapped beside them.

intro:
The final battle — 71 BC

Crassus blocks the road ahead near Paestum. Repeated battles and separations have thinned the army, and Pompey is returning to Italy with another Roman force. The space in which we can march is closing.

Take Paestum and break the positions around it. Bring the surviving groups into one attack before the Romans can hold us here for the next army to arrive. This is the road we have left.
